title: Enlargement and reduction of a plane figure
summary: Apply enlargement and reduction to lengths, coordinates, perimeter and area.
objectives: Enlarge coordinates about a stated centre.
Distinguish linear and area scale factors.
Reverse an enlargement to recover original measurements.

blocks.text: For an enlargement with centre C and factor k, the image point lies on the line through C and the original point. Its directed displacement from C is multiplied by k.

An enlargement with centre C and scale factor k maps each point P along line CP so that vector CP′=k vector CP. On a coordinate grid, P′=C+k(P−C). Positive fractional factors create reductions while preserving direction from the centre.

About the origin, multiply both coordinates by k. About another centre, subtract the centre coordinates, scale the displacement, then add the centre back. Linear dimensions use |k| and areas use k². The centre, object point and image point must be collinear.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: Point P = (2, 3) is enlarged about the origin by scale factor 4. Find P′.

sections.verification_note: Check that every side and angle was matched in the stated corresponding order.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: Point P=(6,4) is enlarged by scale factor 1/2 about C=(2,−2). Find P′.

content.text: The displacement from C to P is (6−2,4−(−2))=(4,6).

sections.verification_note: P′ lies halfway from C to P, so C, P′ and P are collinear.

blocks.text: Do not multiply the coordinates directly unless the centre is the origin. Scale both horizontal and vertical displacements. An area factor is the square of the linear factor, even for a reduction.

prompt.text: A 12 cm side is reduced by scale factor 1/3. Find the image length.

blocks.text: Write the correspondence first, use one consistent scale factor, preserve equal angles, and check whether a length, perimeter or area needs a linear or squared factor.
Before moving on, explain the relevant property in words, show the equation or formula with units, and use the diagram markings to check that every correspondence is consistent.
